references.text: The same command to Moses to meet Pharaoh in the morning by the water, with the same message to let the people go
Repeated command to Moses to rise early and stand before Pharaoh with the message 'Let my people go so they may serve me'
First time Moses and Aaron deliver the message 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Let my people go, so they may hold a feast for me'
The same wording 'Thus says the Lord: Let my people go, so they may serve me'
The Lord's command to Moses to go to Pharaoh with the message to let the people go free so they may serve him
Repeated message to Pharaoh with the wording 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go so they may serve me'
God instructs Moses to tell Pharaoh: 'Let my son go, so he may serve me' - the same fundamental demand
The first formulation of the same demand showing the continuity of God's message from the start of the meeting with Pharaoh.
A sharp contrast between God's demand for complete freedom for service and Pharaoh's attempt to limit this service to Egypt.
A contrast where Pharaoh tries to restrict the service by demanding that possessions remain, in opposition to God's demand for full liberation.
Moses' confirmation that God's demand for freedom to sacrifice/serve cannot be fulfilled through Pharaoh's compromises.
